children: Rica Bhattacharyya Mumbai: Reliance Industries-backed Strand Life Sciences is targeting a major share of India's potential market for early cancer detection over the next five years, as it looks to scale its proprietary blood-based CancerSpot screening test beyond its initial clinical validation. The company estimates a 2,600 crore addressable opportunity at just 5% adoption, based on an eligible population of about 52 million people aged 50-75.

In an independent validation cohort from Strand's 1,480-participant case-control study, CancerSpot demonstrated 72% cancer detection sensitivity and a 1.4% false-positive rate. The underlying research was published in the peer-reviewed Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. CancerSpot is intended to complement standard-of-care cancer screenings. Reliance's mandate for Strand is to dramatically bring down the cost of early-stage cancer and genomic testing, making advanced diagnostics more accessible in India.

Strand is working towards bringing the cost of a test below 10,000 (compared with 26,000 now) over the next two years and 1,000 in the long term, with lower-cost reagents, operational efficiencies and scale among the levers, chief executive Ramesh Hariharan said. Reliance executive Nilesh Modi said achieving scale will require not only continued innovation but also the development of indigenous capabilities in genomic sequencing technologies, equipment and reagents. "This is a kind of Jio-fication of genomics and that is something we need to do by bringing down the cost so that more people can have access to it," he added. "India has the opportunity to build globally competitive capabilities in this critical space, while addressing the growing need for affordable and accessible cancer diagnostics," Modi said. Reliance acquired the Bengaluru-based company for 393 crore in 2021. The conglomerate is leveraging Strand Life Sciences for its entry into the emerging areas of specialised healthcare diagnostics and genomic sciences.

title: Strand Life Eyes Market Share in Multi-cancer Early Detection
